content: What is WebUI Framework? WebUI is an HTML-first framework for native server-side rendering. You write templates and CSS, your backend supplies JSON data, and a Rust renderer produces HTML. Add TypeScript and the browser runtime where you need interactions. Start with your first app . You'll render a page using the locally installed npm CLI, then add a working counter. You do not need Rust, a repository checkout, or a production server to follow along. Coming from React? Components, state, events

content: CSS Tokens and Themes Style components with ordinary CSS custom properties. You can define them in your own stylesheets, or use --theme to validate and supply a shared token set. Theming does not scope selectors: Light DOM CSS is global in its owning CSS tree; Shadow DOM provides native isolation. /* my-card.css, using the default Shadow DOM mode */ :host { color : var( -- text-primary ); background : var( -- surface-page ); } Configure a theme Theme files map token names without -- to CSS value

Source and bundled apps render through Rust without shipping Node or a browser engine. An optional Rust host can instead show an existing loopback HTTP application. The target machine still needs the platform's webview and runtime prerequisites. They are template syntax, not JavaScript expressions or custom elements you register yourself. < if condition = " items.length " > < ul > < for each = " item in items " > < li >{{item.name}}</ li > </ for > </ ul > </ if > Available Directives Choose the directive for the task: <if> Conditional Rendering - Conditionally render content based on expressions <for> Loop Iteration - Iterate over collections to generate r

content: Attribute Directives Use an ordinary binding for an attribute value, ? for conditional presence, or : to pass a value to a child DOM property. Simple Dynamic Attributes Use {{}} inside an attribute value to bind it to a state value: < a href = " {{url}} " >{{linkText}}</ a > < img src = " {{imageUrl}} " alt = " {{imageAlt}} " /> Example State: { " url " : "https://example.com", " linkText " : "Visit Example" } Output: < a href = " https://example.com " >Visit Example</ a > A whole-binding attrib
title: Attribute and property bindings

content: Streaming Boundaries <boundary> marks a complete region that WebUI can render, flush, and hydrate before the rest of the response arrives. It is a compile-time directive and does not create a DOM wrapper. Use it with a host's progressive streaming API and the browser streaming coordinator; adding the directive alone does not turn an ordinary render into a progressively hydrated response. title: Streaming boundaries

content: <for> Loop Directive Use <for each="item in items"> to repeat HTML for each array item. The directive itself adds no DOM wrapper. Basic Usage < for each = " item in items " > < div class = " item " > < h3 >{{item.title}}</ h3 > < p >{{item.description}}</ p > </ div > </ for > Each iteration binds item to the current value. Missing or empty arrays render no items. For lists that reorder, use explicit keys to keep DOM and component state attached to the same item. Using the Loop Variable The loop
title: Lists and loops

content: <if> Conditional Directive Use <if condition="..."> to include a region when its condition is truthy. The directive does not create an extra DOM element. Basic Usage < if condition = " isLoggedIn " > < div class = " welcome " >Welcome back, {{username}}!</ div > </ if > The welcome message renders when isLoggedIn is truthy in the current state. content: Lazy Component Policy Defer offscreen browser work with attributes on a component's root <template> . Rendering and hydration are separate: rendering is layout and paint; hydration attaches bindings and listeners. Hydration explains lifecycle behavior, while Performance explains when deferral is worthwhile. content: Text Bindings Insert state with {{path}} . Use triple braces only for trusted HTML. These bindings read values; they do not evaluate arbitrary JavaScript, call functions, or perform arithmetic. Escaped Signals: {{}} The double curly braces syntax ( {{}} ) inserts a value from the state object with HTML escaping applied: < p >Hello, {{user.name}}!</ p > HTML characters in the value are escaped so they display as text rather than markup.
